[CONCLUSIONS]: Universal tumour testing strategies for guiding germline genetic testing of people with incident CRC for LS in Australia are likely to be cost-effective compared with no testing. Universal germline gene panel testing would not currently be cost-effective.

key_findings.finding: The directly relevant economic evaluation is Mvundura et al., “Fourfold increased detection of Lynch syndrome by raising age limit for tumour genetic testing from 50 to 70 years is cost-effective” (Annals of Oncology, 2014; PMID 25081898). It compared tumor testing for CRC diagnosed at age ≤70 years versus ≤50 years, using probabilistic efficacy and cost-effectiveness decision models based on real-life data, with cascade testing of relatives. Raising the threshold identified approximately four times as many Lynch syndrome patients; the number needed to test per carrier increased from 19 to 42, and testing cost per carrier from €4,837 to €9,437. Including cascade screening, the incremental cost was €2,703 per additional life-year gained, which the authors judged highly cost-effective under Dutch thresholds. The authors concluded that all CRC tumors diagnosed at age ≤70 should be tested.
